drhp.business: The Company manufactures and supplies sheet metal components, frames, long members and assemblies for automotive and railway customers within India. Under Ind AS 108 it is engaged in a single business segment and operates primarily under a single geographic location, India, with a long-standing tier-1 relationship with its principal customer Tata Motors in the medium- and heavy-duty commercial-vehicle category. It is broadening into adjacent segments including railway fabrication and electric commercial vehicles.

risks.note: The Risk Management Committee lists this as a key risk; revenue from a single major customer accounted for Rs 46,111.30 lakhs of revenue from operations during the year. Mitigation is only partial - a long-standing tier-1 relationship, multi-product engagement, and broadening into adjacent segments (railway fabrication, electric commercial vehicles).
risks.risk: Customer concentration - a single OEM accounts for the majority of revenue

risks.note: The Indian CV cycle is inherently cyclical and end-demand can be affected by macroeconomic conditions, freight-rate movements and upstream cost transmission into truck prices; order flow is also lumpy. Managed through deep customer engagement, multi-product positioning across CV and railway segments, and a prudent capital structure that supports operations through cyclical troughs.
risks.risk: Demand cyclicality and end-market risk in the Indian CV cycle

risks.note: Commercial arrangements with principal customers operate on a pass-through basis - steel and other principal raw-material price increases are passed on to customers and decreases passed back - so raw-material volatility is not a direct risk to margin. The live channel is indirect: sustained raw-material inflation raises truck prices for end customers and softens end-demand, and is monitored under demand cyclicality.
risks.risk: Indirect raw-material risk through end-demand, rather than direct margin risk

risks.note: Management states the long-term shift may render certain frame architectures obsolete or force them to evolve - a structural threat to the Company's core frame and long-member product set. The stated response is investing ahead of these transitions through quality, process and customer-engagement programmes.
risks.risk: Technological transition to EV, alternative-fuel and hydrogen-ICE platforms

risks.note: These transitions may require platform-level redesigns and capacity retooling, and regulatory transition costs are listed among the threats as new emission and safety standards come into force.
risks.risk: Regulatory transition costs - BS6 Phase II execution, AC-cabin mandates and ADAS rollout

risks.note: Conflict in West Asia (the US-Iran-Israel conflict) and constraints on key shipping routes, notably the Strait of Hormuz, drive volatility in oil, diesel and bought-out component costs and threaten supply of critical bought-out parts. Management describes itself as in a wait-and-watch posture on how this transmits into fleet operating economics and truck buying behaviour.

The auditors designated inventory a key audit matter: large quantities held across plants in a customer-specific industry, with slow-moving or damaged inventory arising from model discontinuation or excess production accumulated at different locations, and a possibility of gaps between actual and recorded raw-material consumption across product variants.
risks.risk: Inventory obsolescence in a customer-specific manufacturing model (statutory auditors' key audit matter)

risks.note: Announced corporate transactions at the principal customer's parent group will over time reshape the supplier ecosystem and raise the quality bar for tier-1 suppliers. Management frames this as an opportunity for those investing ahead of the curve, but for a supplier with majority revenue from that OEM it is equally a structural re-qualification risk.
risks.risk: Supplier-ecosystem restructuring at the principal customer's parent group
